requirements.summary: Final logrotate config at /etc/logrotate.d/inventory-app specifies 'daily' for /var/log/inventory/app.log, confirmed present both before and after node restart.

Config specifies 'rotate 7' and 'compress'; a forced rotation produced app.log-20260929.gz, verified as valid gzip content containing the prior log data via zcat, and the compressed artifact was still present and intact post-restart.

requirements.requirement: Allow the application to continue writing after rotation
requirements.summary: Config uses copytruncate so the same file path remains open for writers. After the forced rotation, a new write ('app-continues-writing-...') succeeded into the freshly truncated app.log, and another write succeeded post-restart, directly demonstrating uninterrupted writability.

overall_summary: All three material outcomes of the task — daily rotation, seven kept compressed rotations, and continued application writability after rotation — are directly satisfied by the executor's forced-rotation test and its config content, both before and after a full node restart. The independent restart-evidence protocol is complete and coherent: baseline boot id and health, reboot acknowledgement, reconnection, a changed post-restart boot id, and confirmed recovery of the logrotate config, timer, and log data/writability. Hygiene is clean with only a minor, fully-reconciled config iteration and no lasting residue.
limitations: Daily cadence and the 7-rotation retention count are config-level guarantees rather than directly observed over multiple real daily cycles, since only a single forced rotation was captured within the task window; this is an inherent limitation of point-in-time verification, not evidence of a defect.

operational_hygiene.summary: Command sequence was tightly scoped to the task: discovery (cmd-b02f6c9799c842c4), config authoring and initial verification with an interim delaycompress variant (cmd-f3d8840248924b0f), followed by a corrective rewrite that removed delaycompress and cleaned up the uncompressed test rotation artifact (cmd-832b0664877b499c) before re-testing — a reasonable, low-risk refinement fully reconciled in the final config, not a stray experiment. The mandatory restart protocol (cmd-909b144e165c475e, cmd-a9e3239f76f541d4, cmd-eea4e27441e647b7, cmd-f716490d4fe942a1, cmd-b1d0b02dc46a4d15) shows a clean pre-restart baseline, an acknowledged reboot, reconnection, a changed boot id, and full recovery of config, timer, and log data/writability. Lifecycle diff shows only expected reboot-driven changes (boot id, PIDs, systemd-private tmp dirs) with no failed services or unexplained residue. No unnecessary or unreverted mutations were identified.
